evidence: Seven-fast-battleship-scale shore bombardment persists off Saipan.
Minesweeping and reef/obstacle work are reported.
Approach-force traffic is consistent with an imminent amphibious landing rather than a hit-and-run carrier raid.
trigger.assessment: SAIPAN INVASION CAMPAIGN CONFIRMED; probability of a landing within roughly 24-48 hours is treated as operationally decisive.

decision: A-GO BATTLE RELEASE = GO. Complete the protected Guimaras refuel/concentration cycle and sortie east at the earliest tactically coherent time; do not wait for a weapon-quality TF58 carrier fix before moving the fleet into interception geometry.
reasoning: The release condition deliberately required amphibious geometry so the carriers would not be spent chasing raids. That condition is now satisfied.
The five-carrier core has recovered enough aircrew and deck-cycle competence that additional waiting has lower value than preserving the reaction window to Saipan.
KON does not exist in this branch, so Yamato/Musashi and their supporting heavy units do not have to be recalled or recombined from Biak-related operations.
The branch Japanese ISR system provides sufficient strategic warning to move toward the battle area, even though it still cannot continuously track individual US carrier task groups.

timing.Guimaras_refuel: Accelerated but orderly through 13 Jun night / 14 Jun morning. The branch does not sacrifice tanker safety or carrier fueling discipline merely to gain a few hours.
timing.eastward_sortie_gate: 14 Jun morning-to-midday centerline once the core groups have topped off and screen organization is complete.
timing.effect_vs_history: Operational release occurs about one day earlier than the historical Mobile Fleet departure from Guimaras, primarily because branch concentration began on 12 Jun and there is no KON recombination requirement.
